items.title: Losing Sight, Finding My Voice with Sayyida Victoria Hillard
items.description: Sayyida Victoria Hillard joins Cazerny Bussey to talk about motherhood, confidence, Blind Professionals Network, and building a stronger community.
items.text: When Sayyida Victoria Hillard lost her sight at 30, she was raising four children and trying to understand what life would look like next. In her conversation with Cazerny Bussey on the Even Though I’m Blind Experience podcast, she speaks openly about that adjustment—and the confidence, purpose, and community she has built since. “I like me better as a blind woman,” she shares. That statement comes with a story. Sayyida talks about grieving her sight, learning to do things differently, and recognizing that her knowledge, skills, and abilities were still hers. She also describes how blindness changed the way she connects with people, giving conversations more weight than appearances. Her experiences as a mother of five bring another dimension to the episode. Her older children lived through the early adjustment alongside her. Her youngest, born after she became blind, grew up with a mother who had become more confident in navigating everyday life. Sayyida shares both sides with honesty and humor. Creating the Support She Needed Sayyida’s community work began with a need she recognized personally. She wanted a place where blind professionals could talk with peers about employment, workplace barriers, career goals, and the pressure to prove themselves. In 2019, she created the support group that became Blind Professionals Network. During the episode, she explains how that group grew into workshops, training, and a wider network of people committed to helping each other succeed. Today, she serves as BPN’s founder and executive director. Its programs and services are free. Her work also includes BPN Workplace Solutions, which provides professional services and creates employment opportunities for blind individuals, along with development coaching through Better Blind Insight and Clear Vision Coaching. Through Blind Table Talk, she makes space for conversations, stories, and resources that connect the blind and visually impaired community with one another and with the wider world. More Collaboration, More Opportunity One of the clearest messages in this episode is Sayyida’s call for collaboration. She believes the community benefits when organizations support each other, share resources, and recognize that no single organization can meet every need. She and Cazerny also discuss independence, raising blind children with opportunities to participate, and the cost of holding yourself back because of other people’s opinions. Her reminder to listeners is direct: never dim your shine because of what you think others might say. Learn more about Sayyida’s businesses, coaching, podcasts, and community work at SayyidaVictoria.com . Check Out the Full Episode Here Listen to Losing Sight, Finding My Voice with Sayyida Victoria Hillard on your preferred platform: Apple Podcasts Spotify Amazon Music

items.title: Bridging Two Worlds: Even Though I’m Blind and HODB Are Expanding What Inclusive Media Can Look Like
items.description: Even Though I’m Blind, Inc. and HODB Mag & Media are bridging blind-centered media with broader culture, creativity and community to expand awareness, representation and inclusion.
items.text: What happens when media created to amplify the blind and visually impaired community connects with a broader platform built around culture, entertainment, entrepreneurship, creativity and community? You create a bridge. That is what is developing through the partnership between Even Though I’m Blind, Inc. (ETIB) and Hot On Da Block (HODB) Mag & Media . These are two distinct platforms with different audiences and different lanes, but there is power in those lanes intersecting. Even Though I’m Blind was built to amplify blind and visually impaired voices, create opportunities, connect people with resources, challenge perceptions, and expand the way the world understands blindness, ability, leadership and independence. HODB Mag & Media , led by Johnny Torres, has built a broader cultural platform highlighting artists, entrepreneurs, filmmakers, creators, community leaders and people whose stories deserve to be heard. HODB has expanded into a multi-lane media ecosystem spanning arts and culture, current cultural coverage, filmmaking, creator experiences and community initiatives. That makes this partnership about much more than cross-promotion. It is about crossing communities. Taking the Conversation Beyond Blindness Spaces One of the challenges with awareness is that important conversations can sometimes remain inside the communities already having them. Blind people talk about blindness. Disability organizations talk about accessibility. Advocates talk to other advocates. Those conversations are necessary, but real cultural change requires something more. The conversation also has to reach people who were not already looking for it. That is where collaborations like ETIB and HODB can become powerful. When a story about blindness appears alongside stories about music, business, culture, film, entrepreneurship and everyday life, blindness is no longer being treated as a separate conversation. It becomes part of the larger human conversation. And that is inclusion. Cazerny Bussey Featured by HODB That bridge can already be seen through a recent HODB feature with Cazerny Bussey, founder and CEO of Even Though I’m Blind, Inc. In the conversation, Bussey speaks about growing up, losing his eyesight, the experiences that shaped him, and his journey toward becoming an advocate and building a platform dedicated to changing perspectives surrounding blindness. But the conversation goes beyond one man’s story. It gets into the reason Even Though I’m Blind exists. ETIB was never created to ask the world to feel sorry for blind people. It was created to challenge assumptions, create opportunities, amplify voices, connect communities and demonstrate that blindness is one characteristic of a person, not the boundary of that person’s potential. Watch the HODB Feature https://www.instagram.com/reel/DdXu_Vwh-bs/ Cazerny Bussey speaks with HODB about his journey, blindness and the mission of Even Though I’m Blind, Inc. Two Media Ecosystems, One Larger Opportunity The partnership between HODB and Even Though I’m Blind represents something that we believe should happen more often. Communities should intersect. Audiences should overlap. Platforms should collaborate. HODB has developed an ecosystem centered around creators, culture, storytelling, entrepreneurship, filmmaking and community. Even Though I’m Blind has developed an ecosystem centered around advocacy, media, music, storytelling, resources, accessibility and opportunities for blind and visually impaired people. Neither platform has to become the other. That is precisely the point. Each brings something different to the table. When those audiences meet, HODB’s community can encounter perspectives from the blind and visually impaired community in an organic cultural environment. At the same time, ETIB’s community gains another connection to creators, entrepreneurs, artists and opportunities beyond disability-centered spaces. That is how awareness grows beyond a campaign. It becomes part of culture. Inclusion Is Bigger Than Representation Representation matters. But representation is only the beginning. Real inclusion means blind creators being part of entertainment. Blind entrepreneurs being part of business conversations. Blind musicians being part of music conversations. Blind leaders being part of leadership conversations. It means blind people being discussed not only when the subject is blindness, but when the subject is life . That is one of the larger ideas behind Even Though I’m Blind. Our goal is not to build walls around the blind community. It is to build doors. Doors into media. Doors into creativity. Doors into entrepreneurship. Doors into technology. Doors into entertainment. Doors into conversations where our perspectives may have historically been missing. Partnerships help open those doors. Changing Perspective Requires Reaching New People If we only speak to people who already understand accessibility, we cannot expect awareness to expand very far. If we only tell blind stories to audiences already connected to blindness, we limit the number of people those stories can reach. Changing perspective means entering new rooms. It means telling authentic stories without reducing people to disability. It means giving broader audiences opportunities to see blind people as founders, parents, musicians, executives, creators, neighbors, leaders, innovators and human beings. That is why this collaboration matters. HODB and ETIB do not have identical missions. They do not need to. Their differences are exactly what make the bridge valuable. This Is What Building the Bridge Looks Like There is a future where disability media and mainstream media do not feel like two completely separate worlds. items.title: Access Now, FUTURES, and Alicia Grace’s Story
items.description: Learn how Access Now and FUTURES are creating accessibility, community, and opportunity, and hear Alicia Grace share her experience as a blind actor.
items.text: Accessibility can open doors to opportunity, independence, connection, and a stronger sense of belonging. What Access Now Does Access Now helps people find important accessibility information through its connected platform, app, and map. Users can discover and review places based on their accessibility features, including restaurants, hotels, shops, attractions, transit locations, parks, and trails. This information helps people plan with greater confidence and find welcoming places in their communities and around the world. Visit Access Now: https://accessnow.com/ Explore the Access Now map: https://map.accessnow.com/ Download the Access Now app: Apple App Store Google Play FUTURES Creates Community and Opportunity FUTURES is an AccessStudio program for Disabled and neurodivergent young people in Canada between the ages of 18 and 30. The 12-week program gives participants the opportunity to meet regularly with the same cohort and explore identity, disability justice, community, creativity, leadership, and social impact. Participants are encouraged to reflect on their experiences, build confidence, connect with others, and consider how they can create meaningful change. FUTURES is built around the understanding that Disabled and neurodivergent young people already possess valuable knowledge and life experience. The program helps give that experience structure, direction, and a supportive community. Learn more about FUTURES: https://studio.accessnow.com/futures Alicia Grace’s Experience Alicia Grace participated in FUTURES and shared her story on the Even Though I’m Blind Experience Podcast. As a blind actor, Alicia spoke about entering rooms where people realize she may be the first visually impaired actor they have ever encountered. That experience reflects why representation and access are so important. Alicia is pursuing her goals, building her career, and helping others see blind people as talented professionals and creators. Her experience also shows the human impact of programs like FUTURES. When people find a community that understands them and gives them room to grow, they can gain confidence, recognize their strengths, and move closer to the future they envision. Follow Alicia Grace on Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/aliciagraceofficial/ Watch the Full Conversation Hear Alicia Grace discuss her experience, acting, representation, and the importance of opportunity on the Even Though I’m Blind Experience Podcast: Watch the full conversation on YouTube Learn more about Access Now and discover how accessibility information and inclusive programs can help create more opportunities for Disabled people and their communities.

items.title: Busta Rhymes Shares a Powerful Exchange with Even Though I’m Blind
items.description: During a SiriusXM and Pandora listening party, Busta Rhymes shared a powerful exchange with ETIB CEO and Founder Cazerny Bussey about how blind people envision the world.
items.text: Recently, Even Though I’m Blind, Inc. attended a listening party for Busta Rhymes hosted by Danielle Graziano at SiriusXM and Pandora in New York City. During a powerful exchange, ETIB CEO and Founder Cazerny Bussey explained how losing his eyesight forced him to experience life through vision beyond sight. Busta Rhymes shared that he could not imagine how blind people envision things without relying on their eyes. He wondered what blind people see and acknowledged that those circumstances may cause people to see the world in a deeper way. Busta also expressed that he is always willing to learn. We honor Busta Rhymes for his lasting contributions to hip-hop and thank SiriusXM, Pandora, and Danielle Graziano for hosting this meaningful moment. Watch the Exchange Watch the full exchange on YouTube . Support the Album Support Busta Rhymes and J Dilla’s DILLAGENCE II : Listen on Apple Music | Listen on Spotify

items.title: Access in Focus 2026: Blind Voices, Accessible Entertainment and the Power of Being Seen
items.description: Even Though I’m Blind covers Lighthouse Guild’s Access in Focus at Lincoln Center, featuring Lachi, Nicole Harris, Petr Kucheryavyy, Spectrum Access and a special appearance by hip-hop icon Special Ed.
items.text: By Even Though I’m Blind On Saturday, August 8, 2026, Even Though I’m Blind covered Access in Focus: Blind Perspectives on Entertainment Accessibility , an evening presented by Lighthouse Guild in partnership with Spectrum at Lincoln Center’s Stanley H. Kaplan Penthouse in New York City. The conversation brought together blind professionals working at the intersection of entertainment, technology, creativity and advocacy. But the evening carried a message larger than accessibility alone. Blind and visually impaired people deserve the opportunity not only to experience entertainment fully, but to create it, shape it, work within it and have their voices heard. Kiana Glanton: Hosting the Conversation With Lived Experience Guiding the evening was Kiana Glanton , who hosted Access in Focus and brought her own lived experience, advocacy and professional work into the room. Glanton serves as Development and Special Projects Manager at Lighthouse Guild and is also a lead advocate and ambassador for Adaptive Athletics. A Stony Brook University graduate, she has represented the United States in blind baseball and has used both sport and storytelling to expand ideas about what is possible for people who are blind or have low vision. Her connection to the evening’s accessibility message extends beyond the stage. Glanton and her daughter, Kali, were featured in a Spectrum commercial demonstrating the Spectrum Access app . The commercial shows how audio description allows Kiana to experience television and movies alongside her daughter, turning accessible technology into something deeply personal: the ability for a family to share entertainment together. Watch Kiana Glanton and her daughter Kali in the Spectrum Access commercial Kiana’s role as host made her an especially fitting voice to connect the panel’s themes. Her work reflects the same principle at the heart of Access in Focus: accessibility is strongest when people with lived experience are not simply included in the audience, but are helping lead the conversation. Kiana Glanton of Lighthouse Guild hosting Access in Focus 2026. Three Perspectives, One Larger Conversation The featured panel brought together Lachi, Nicole Harris and Petr Kucheryavyy , each approaching accessibility from a different part of the entertainment landscape. Their perspectives connected around a common idea: access is not simply about accommodating people after something has already been created. It is about ensuring disabled people have meaningful places throughout the culture as audiences, professionals, creators and decision-makers. Lachi: Representation Changes What We Believe Is Possible Lachi is an award-winning recording artist, author, media personality and Disability Culture advocate. She also founded RAMPD, Recording Artists and Music Professionals with Disabilities, to advance disability inclusion at the highest levels of the music industry. Lachi at Access in Focus 2026. During the panel, Lachi spoke about the importance of representation . Growing up legally blind, she did not have enough examples showing her what a blind or low-vision person could become. Seeing people who share parts of our identities succeeding can fundamentally change what we imagine for ourselves. Her message underscored why representation cannot stop at simply placing disabled people on screen. It matters behind microphones, in recording studios, in writers’ rooms, in executive offices and everywhere entertainment is created. That theme also runs through Lachi’s newly released album, Magnificent , a project celebrating disability, neurodivergence, identity and belonging. Representation can become permission. When people see someone like themselves creating, leading and succeeding, their own possibilities become easier to imagine. Nicole Harris: Stop Waiting for Perfect and Start Creating Nicole Harris brought the creator’s perspective to the conversation. Her message was refreshingly practical: create, post, be yourself and keep going. Nicole Harris at Access in Focus 2026. For aspiring creators, waiting for the perfect video, perfect draft, perfect opportunity or perfect version of yourself can become its own barrier. The alternative is authenticity. Harris encouraged creators to stop remaining only on the other side of the screen, scrolling through everyone else’s work, and begin putting their own ideas into the world. Her larger message was that consistency and authenticity can create opportunities, communities and even income. You do not necessarily need an elaborate production to begin. You need a voice, something meaningful to communicate and the willingness to use it. Harris is a blind content creator and founder of the Love The Hope Project. Readers can follow Nicole Harris and explore her work here . For blind creators especially, accessible technology has dramatically lowered some of the barriers between having an idea and publishing it to the world. The next barrier can simply be believing that your voice belongs there. Petr Kucheryavyy and Spectrum Access: Making Entertainment Something Everyone Can Experience Technology became a major part of the evening through Petr Kucheryavyy , Senior Director of Outreach, Communications, Learning and Development and product owner of the Spectrum Access app for Spectrum’s Accessibility team. Petr Kucheryavyy of Spectrum at Access in Focus 2026. Spectrum Access addresses a deceptively simple question: What if a blind person wants to enjoy the same movie as everyone else in the room without forcing everyone else to change how they watch it? The free app lets users access audio description for supported movies and television programs. A blind viewer can listen to description through their device or headphones while experiencing the program alongside everyone else. items.title: Even Though I’m Blind, Inc. Joins Access Information News as a Sponsored Organization
items.description: Even Though I’m Blind, Inc. joins Access Information News as a sponsored organization, expanding ETIB’s reach across the disability, accessibility, advocacy, and inclusion community.
items.text: Even Though I’m Blind, Inc. is proud to announce a new sponsorship relationship with Access Information News, expanding our ability to share our mission, programs, stories, and advocacy with a wider disability community. Beginning August 10, 2026, Even Though I’m Blind, Inc. will join the Access Information News sponsor community. Access Information News reaches more than 45,000 verified weekly subscribers interested in disability, accessibility, inclusion, technology, advocacy, and information that impacts the disability community. For Even Though I’m Blind, this relationship represents another opportunity to expand the reach of the work we are building. Our mission has always been bigger than simply talking about blindness. We are building platforms that give blind and visually impaired people greater visibility, create opportunities for creators and advocates, connect people with resources, and challenge the way the world thinks about ability and leadership. Through this sponsorship, Even Though I’m Blind will receive ongoing visibility through Access Information News and become part of the PWD Media Co op, a network focused on amplifying disability voices through collective reach. The sponsorship also creates opportunities for us to highlight ETIB programs, initiatives, events, media, and community resources throughout the coming year. Access Information News publisher Aaron Di Blasi has also written a welcome feature introducing Even Though I’m Blind and sharing the story behind our organization and its name. The feature will be shared across the PWD Media Co op during the coming weeks. Read the Access Information News Feature We are grateful to Aaron and Access Information News for welcoming Even Though I’m Blind into their community and for recognizing the value of the work we are building. This is not simply about gaining exposure. It is about building relationships, connecting communities, and creating more pathways for blind and visually impaired voices to be heard. As Even Though I’m Blind continues to grow, partnerships like this help us carry that mission further. We look forward to what comes next. Cazerny Bussey Founder and CEO Even Though I’m Blind, Inc. The Leading Global Voice for the Blind and Visually Impaired Empowering Vision Worldwide

items.title: Trying Glide for the First Time: How AI Mobility Technology Gave Me a New Sense of Confidence
items.description: Cazerny Bussey shares his first experience with Glide, Glidance’s AI-powered mobility device, at the 2026 NFB Convention—and explains its features, promise, limitations, price, and availability.
items.text: What happens when a new mobility tool does more than help you move—when it changes how supported and confident you feel? I had the opportunity to find out when I tried Glide for the first time at the 2026 National Federation of the Blind Convention in Austin, Texas. I am Cazerny Bussey, founder and CEO of Even Though I’m Blind, Inc. As a blind man, advocate, artist, author, and leader, I pay close attention to technology that can expand independence without taking away a person’s choice, identity, or control. My first experience with Glide was brief, but the feeling it created was immediate. Cazerny Bussey experiences Glide for the first time at the 2026 NFB National Convention in Austin, Texas. Watch My First Experience With Glide Watch Cazerny Bussey share his first experience using Glide at the 2026 NFB National Convention in Austin, Texas. Watch the Glide Video on Facebook “I will go everywhere with it. Y’all should get the Glide!” Cazerny Bussey The Moment Glide Surprised Me The National Federation of the Blind held its 2026 National Convention from July 3 through July 8 in Austin. The convention brought blind people, advocates, families, educators, organizations, and technology developers together around opportunity, community, and independence. When I tried Glide, I did not expect such a short demonstration to create such a strong emotional response. As the device guided me, I felt more than directional assistance. I felt as though I had a guide, a friend, and support right beside me. That sense of support gave me confidence. This matters because independent mobility is not only about reaching a destination. It is also about how secure, informed, comfortable, and empowered a person feels during the journey. What Is Glide? Glide is an AI-powered mobility device developed by Glidance for people who are blind or have low vision. Glidance describes it as a third primary mobility option alongside the white cane and guide dog. The lightweight device has two wheels on the ground, a telescoping stem, and an ergonomic handle. The user gently pushes it forward while walking. Using cameras, sensors, artificial intelligence, autonomous steering, and braking, Glide is designed to guide the user along a route, maintain a line of travel, identify important targets, and respond to obstacles. Glide is not a self-driving vehicle that carries the user. The person remains on foot and controls the pace while the device provides physical guidance, audio information, and haptic feedback through the handle. Key Features Glidance Is Developing Indoor and outdoor navigation: Designed for familiar routes and new environments. Obstacle and hazard response: Intended to detect and steer around objects, drop-offs, curbs, potholes, and other hazards. Line maintenance: Helps the user continue in a purposeful direction without unnecessary veering. Target finding: Designed to help locate doors, elevators, stairs, and other useful destinations. Audio and haptic feedback: Communicates information through sound and touch. Intersection support: Glidance says Glide can help identify crosswalks and maintain direction during street crossings. Portable design: The device weighs less than eight pounds and uses a telescoping handle. All-day battery: Glidance lists up to six or more hours of active use, with standby time, on one charge. USB-C charging: It can be charged from a standard outlet with a USB-C cable. Weather resistance: Glide is described as water resistant and suitable for use in rain. Software improvements: Over-the-air updates allow features and AI models to improve over time. Important Practical and Safety Information Promising technology should be discussed with both excitement and honesty. According to Glidance’s current frequently asked questions , Glide is still being developed and tested with members of the blind and low-vision community. Availability: As of July 2026, Glidance says its preorder program is closed and invites interested people to join the waitlist for future availability. Price: Glidance currently lists an initial retail price of $1,499 USD. Pricing may change. Stairs: Glide is designed to guide a user to a staircase and announce arrival, but the user must carry the device up or down the stairs. Balance-support devices: Glidance advises that Glide is not designed to be used with a support cane, walker, rollator, or wheelchair. Training and judgment: Every person’s mobility needs are different. Users should follow official onboarding and safety guidance and consult an Orientation and Mobility professional when appropriate. Changing specifications: Features, timelines, pricing, and availability can change as testing and development continue. The Story Behind Glidance Glidance was founded by Amos Miller , a blind technologist who lost his sight in his twenties. Miller previously worked as a product executive at Microsoft Research and founded Microsoft’s Soundscape navigation app. His lived experience and technology background helped shape Glidance’s focus on independence, freedom, and autonomous wayfinding. That origin is significant. Inclusive technology is strongest when blind and low-vision people are not treated only as consumers at the end of the process, but are involved in imagining, testing, improving, and leading the work from the beginning. Why This Technology Matters Blind people are not a single group with identical preferences. Some people rely on white canes. Some use guide dogs. Some use both at different times. Others may want another option. The real value of innovation is not forcing one answer on everyone; it is expanding the number of meaningful choices people can make. Glide represents a larger movement toward assistive technology that is intelligent, responsive, portable, and shaped around real life. Its potential is not simply in the hardware. Its potential is in helping people approach unfamiliar spaces, crowded public areas, airports, stores, workplaces, and everyday

items.title: Angela Harris Is Changing What Inclusion Looks Like in Fashion
items.description: Angela Harris, founder of the Imperfektly Made Fashion Show and Foundation, is creating visibility, confidence, and opportunity for blind and visually impaired models through style, access, and representation.
items.text: Some people talk about impact. Angela Harris is living it. As the founder of the Imperfektly Made Fashion Show and Foundation, Angela is creating more than a runway. She is creating visibility, confidence, opportunity, and a real sense of belonging for blind and visually impaired models who deserve to be seen in every sense of the word. Her story is powerful because it is real. After losing her vision following brain tumor surgery, Angela had to rebuild life in a way most people cannot fully imagine. But instead of shrinking, she expanded. Instead of stepping back, she stepped into something bigger. What came out of that journey is a movement rooted in style, dignity, access, and representation. More Than a Runway The Imperfektly Made Fashion Show stands out because it is not built on sympathy. It is built on presence, confidence, and excellence. It shows the world that blind and visually impaired people are not defined by limitation. They are creators, leaders, visionaries, and trendsetters. Angela has helped shape a space where models can walk with pride, where inclusion is not treated like a favor, and where community meets purpose in a real way. What makes Angela connect with people is her honesty. She speaks openly about the hard parts, the awkward moments, the adjustment, the growth, and the determination it takes to keep going when life changes. That kind of truth reaches people. It reminds people that challenges do not erase purpose. Sometimes they reveal it. A Story Rooted in Strength Her work also extends beyond the runway. Angela is the author of Life as I See It: Finding strength through adversity , a book that reflects the heart of her journey and the mindset that keeps her moving forward. For anyone who wants to hear more of Angela’s voice and story firsthand, her full conversation on the Even Though I’m Blind Experience Podcast is available here: Watch the episode on YouTube It is a powerful listen for anyone who wants a deeper look at her journey, her mission, and the movement she is building through Imperfektly Made. Angela Harris is not just building a fashion show. She is building proof that inclusion can be stylish, powerful, and deeply human. And in a world that still has a lot to learn about accessibility and representation, that kind of work matters. Learn More To learn more, visit imperfektlymade.com . For sponsorship or direct inquiries, email info@imperfektlymade.com or call 240-416-3741 . For more stories like this featuring amazing blind and visually impaired voices, visit eventhoughimblind.com . https://videopress.com/v/3Jncza2E?resizeToParent=true&cover=true&preloadContent=metadata&useAverageColor=true Angela Harris speaking and sharing her voice, story, and mission.

items.title: Discover the Even Though I’m Blind Experience Podcast, Now Just a Voice Command Away!
items.description: Play the Even Though I’m Blind Experience Podcast with a simple voice command on Alexa or Siri, powerful stories, instantly.
items.text: Welcome to a new way to experience the stories and voices of the blind and visually impaired community. The Even Though I’m Blind Experience Podcast is all about amplifying real, heartfelt conversations that inspire and enlighten. Whether you’re looking for motivation, understanding, or the hottest and most exciting insights in the community, this fast growing podcast is your go to. And now, it’s easier than ever to tune in. Simply say, “Alexa, play the Even Though I’m Blind Experience Podcast,” or ask Siri to do the same. In just a moment, you’ll be listening hands free to stories that matter. From time to time, a story might be chosen to be shared with our audience, powerful voices selected with care. If you feel your story carries that spark, send it to eventhoughimblind@gmail.com and it may just be the one that gets heard. Join us and dive into the conversations that bridge communities and uplift voices. Your next favorite episode is just a voice command away. Play video

Built by and for the blind and visually impaired community, our nonprofit radio platform exists to amplify authentic voices, elevate independent talent, and move the culture […]
items.text: Even Though I’m Blind I Can Still Hear Greatness. In a world full of noise, ETIB Radio stands out with purpose. We’re not just another station we’re a movement. Built by and for the blind and visually impaired community, our nonprofit radio platform exists to amplify authentic voices, elevate independent talent, and move the culture forward with heart. But we’re missing your sound. The Problem You’ve been creating, recording, pushing your music but doors keep closing. You’ve got a message, but not the right platform. You’re tired of being overlooked. We hear you. The Solution ETIB Radio is here to spotlight artists like you raw, talented, and ready. If you’re a singer, rapper, poet, producer, or creative with something real to say, this is your lane. We welcome music and spoken word in styles like: Hip-Hop Gospel R&B Pop Underground Soul Latin Audio storytelling and sound art Submit Your Music No politics. No gatekeeping. Just real people who care about your art. Send your submission directly to our team: Email: eventhoughimblind@gmail.com Subject line: Music Submission [Your Artist Name] Include: MP3 or WAV file Short artist bio Your social media links Optional: Tell us the story behind your track Listen to ETIB Radio Tune in now and hear what sets us apart. We’re here for creators with something to say and something to change. Listen live at: Zeno Radio Link Here Why It Matters ETIB Radio is part of the greater mission of Even Though I’m Blind Inc. An organization committed to inclusivity, creativity, and empowerment. When you submit, you don’t just share a song. You join a mission to elevate underrepresented voices and show the world what real vision sounds like. Ready to be heard? We’re listening. ETIB Radio promo ￼

items.title: About ETIB
items.description: Even Though I’m Blind, Inc. ETIB exists to amplify voices, expand access, spotlight talent, connect people with opportunity, and reshape how the world understands ability, leadership, and […]
items.text: Even Though I’m Blind, Inc. (ETIB) is a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit and a global platform dedicated to empowering blind and visually impaired people through advocacy, accessible media, creativity, education, resources, and community connection. ETIB exists to amplify voices, expand access, spotlight talent, connect people with opportunity, and reshape how the world understands ability, leadership, and impact. Welcome to Even Though I’m Blind Our Mission Our mission is to uplift blind and visually impaired people by creating platforms and experiences that inform, inspire, connect, and open doors. ETIB advances dignity, visibility, accessibility, equity, perseverance, and opportunity without defining people by limitation. What ETIB Does Produces accessible media through ETIB Radio, the ETIB Radio Podcast, the ETIB Experience Podcast, the ETIB Blog, and digital storytelling. Highlights blind and visually impaired creators, artists, advocates, entrepreneurs, students, and leaders. Connects people with businesses, services, programs, and resources through the Community Connect Directory. Creates encouragement, education, advocacy, and community-centered experiences. Builds partnerships with organizations, businesses, schools, funders, media platforms, and community leaders. Who We Serve ETIB serves blind and visually impaired individuals, families, caregivers, creators, students, advocates, entrepreneurs, and resource seekers. We also work with donors, sponsors, schools, nonprofits, businesses, media organizations, accessibility partners, and allies committed to meaningful inclusion. Leadership and Vision ETIB was founded by Cazerny Bussey, a Brooklyn-born recording artist, author, entrepreneur, speaker, advocate, and father. His leadership connects lived experience with creativity, service, strategy, and a commitment to building lasting global impact. Blindness is part of the ETIB story, but it is never presented as a reason for pity. ETIB focuses on vision, capability, purpose, resilience, leadership, and the power to keep moving forward. Our Vision ETIB is building a worldwide ecosystem where blind and visually impaired people are heard, valued, connected, represented, and positioned to lead. Our vision is reflected in our message: The Leading Global Voice for the Blind. Empowering Vision Worldwide. Join ETIB Book a Call With ETIB

items.title: Losing Sight, Finding My Voice with Sayyida Victoria Hillard
items.description: “I like me better as a blind woman.” Sayyida Victoria Hillard joins Cazerny Bussey on the Even Though I’m Blind Experience podcast to explain why. The Blind Table Talk host shares how losing her sight at 30 changed her confidence, her approach to motherhood, and the way she connects with people. She also talks about creating Blind Professionals Network when she couldn’t find the support she needed—and why our community needs more collaboration, less competition, and room for everyone to shine.

items.title: Access Now and FUTURES: Accessibility, Advocacy, and Representation.
items.description: In this episode of the Even Though I’m Blind Experience Podcast, Cazerny Bussey sits down with Joey Florence, Jessica Watkin, and Alicia Grace from Access Now and the FUTURES program. They discuss accessibility, community building, social activism, disability representation, and creating opportunities for young disabled and neurodivergent adults. Alicia shares her experience as a blind actor and filmmaker, including how FUTURES helped her pursue accessibility in the arts. Jessica speaks candidly about pregnancy, medical accessibility, and the experiences blind and visually impaired women face. Joey explains how FUTURES helps participants build confidence, community, leadership, and social impact. This is a meaningful conversation about representation, creativity, advocacy, and building a more accessible world together.

items.title: Blindness didn’t stop Christopher felder calling, it’s sharpened it.
items.description: In this powerful episode of The Even Though I’m Blind Experience, Christopher Felder, also known as The Blind Steppa, opens up about surviving gun violence after being shot three times, losing his sight, battling depression, and finding the strength to keep going. Through faith, purpose, and perseverance, Christopher shares how he turned pain into power and realized that you don’t need sight to do God’s work. This conversation is raw, inspiring, and full of truth for anyone pushing through darkness to find their mission. Tune in, tap in, and remember: vision is bigger than eyesight.

items.description: Esli Ramos pulls back the curtain on everyday school life as a blind student, honest, grounded stories and tactile details that make the experience real. She reveals how she learned to stand up for herself, the moments and choices that turned vulnerability into leadership. Hosted by Cazerny Bussey.

items.title: Big Saint, CEO of the First Blind Run Record Label Speaks Out
items.description: In this powerful conversation, Big Saint opens up about his journey as the CEO of the first blind run record label BMG Blind Money Gang, built to pay and empower artists who are often overlooked in the industry. Together with Cazerny Bussey, they break down the vision, the struggles, and the real moves being made to change the game for blind and visually impaired creatives everywhere. This is more than music, it’s history in the making.

items.title: Your Eyesight Does Not Determine Your Future 💡 Professor Blindie.
items.description: Discover powerful wisdom in this episode of the ETIB Experience Podcast hosted by Cazerny Bussey. Professor Blindie shares the inspiring truth that your eyesight does not determine your future, reminding us that every step you take today can inspire others tomorrow. Whether you’re part of the blind and visually impaired community or simply seeking motivation, this message will uplift and empower you to keep moving forward. 🔥 Don’t forget to like, comment, and follow for more conversations that amplify voices, inspire change, and highlight extraordinary journeys. #Motivation #ETIBExperience #CazernyBussey #ProfessorBlindie #BlindCommunity #Inspiration #Podcast #DisabilityAwareness #LifeLessons #Empowerment

items.title: From Tragedy to Triumph, Paradise & Unique Bless 20 Students.
items.description: Losing a child changes you forever, but for Paradise, it became fuel to give back. In this powerful episode of The Even Though I’m Blind Experience, Paradise and Unique share how they turned pain into purpose, teaming up to bless 20 students with back-to-school essentials. From raw stories of loss to the joy of putting a smile on a child’s face, this is more than a charity drive, it’s a movement of resilience, love, and community. 🎧 Watch now and feel the impact. 🌍 Join the mission: EvenThoughImBlind.com Follow for more stories that inspire action. #CommunityImpact #Inspiration #CharityGiving

items.title: Beat by Beat, My 10-Year-Old Son Teaches a Blind Father About Music, Chess, and Leading by Example
items.description: In this heartfelt episode of the Even Though I’m Blind Experience , host Cazerny Bussey, a blind father, shares an authentic and uplifting conversation with his 10-year-old son, affectionately known as C3. Together, they openly discuss discovering new passions like music production and chess, highlighting C3’s thoughtful insights and natural curiosity. Through their genuine father-son exchange, Cazerny emphasizes the importance of determination, self-discovery, and the power of being a positive role model. This episode deeply resonates with the community, showcasing how impactful guidance and encouragement can empower young minds to confidently pursue their own dreams.
